explainBack.question: Why can't a RatHat text message alone infect an Android phone, and where in the chain does the real danger occur?
explainBack.answer: The message only carries a link to a deceptive download page. Nothing happens unless the person manually downloads and installs the app file outside Google Play, and even then the malware still needs the person to grant Accessibility access before it can read the screen and act inside other apps. The danger sits at those two human approval steps — the sideload install and the Accessibility grant — not in receiving the message.
explainBack.expectedEvidence: An accurate answer must cite the manual-download step outside the Play Store (P002), the persuaded Accessibility activation and what that access enables (P003), and the explicit limit that the report does not prove infection from a message (P002/P007).
explainBack.assessment: The article fully supports this answer: P002 supplies the manual-install dependency and the negation of message-only infection, P003 supplies the Accessibility grant and its capability, and P007 restates the limit. Explain-back succeeds in ordinary language.

unseenTransfer.scenario: A reader's teenager wants a 'free coins mod' for a popular game. A YouTube description links to a site offering the APK; after install, the app displays a screen saying 'Enable Accessibility to activate the mod' and walks through disabling the restricted-settings block.
unseenTransfer.question: Using the article's mechanism, what should the reader conclude about this app before any coins or symptoms appear, and what should they do?
unseenTransfer.answer: The chain matches the article's model exactly: an off-Play sideload followed by a coached Accessibility grant. A game mod has no legitimate need to read the screen and operate other apps, so the Accessibility request itself is the warning sign, regardless of whether anything bad has happened yet. The reader should refuse the grant, not walk around the restricted-settings pause, check whether the developer exists on Google Play, run/keep Play Protect on, and remove the app if flagged or if the developer cannot be verified.
unseenTransfer.expectedEvidence: Application of the sideload-plus-grant model (P002/P003), the restricted-settings 'trust the developer' rule (P005), and the Play/official-source and Play Protect actions (P006).
unseenTransfer.assessment: The article's mechanism transfers cleanly: the reader can classify a novel lure (game mod via video description) and act correctly using only the causal model and checks the article taught. Transfer succeeds.
